claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I have one child I'd like to check eligibility for - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'm assessing eligibility for your son Alex.

Now, let me ask you the first question:

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful information.

**Is Alex still in full-time education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for clarifying that.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status or another immigration status that allows you to reside in the UK?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I live in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Are you responsible for Alex, meaning you are caring for him and he is living with you as part of your household?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. He lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you.

**Does Alex receive any of the following benefits in his own right: Personal Independence Payment (PIP), Disability Living Allowance (DLA), Attendance Allowance, or Armed Forces Independence Payment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification.

**Is there anyone else who is already receiving Child Benefit for Alex, such as another parent or guardian?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've provided:

- Alex is 17 years old
- He is in full-time education (studying for A-levels at sixth form)
- You are a British citizen living in the UK
- Alex lives with you as part of your household
- Alex does not receive any qualifying disabilities benefits
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

You meet all the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit for your son Alex. Children can receive Child Benefit until age 19 if they remain in full-time education, and Alex qualifies under this provision.

Congratulations. You can now proceed with your claim if you haven't already done so. Is there anything else I can help you with?
